title: Tokenomics
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/0/body: **Circulating supply:** tokens you can trade on the market right now. **Total supply:** every token created minus the burned ones, even if they're locked. **Max supply:** the cap it can never go above, like Bitcoin's **21 million**.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/1/prompt: A token has a max supply of 1 billion and a circulating supply of 200 million. What percent of the max supply hasn't entered the market yet?
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/1/explanatio: 200 million means 20% of the 1 billion is circulating, so 80% still has to enter the market in the future. That's a lot of supply on the way.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/2/statement: All coins have a fixed max supply, like Bitcoin.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/2/explanatio: Many networks have no fixed cap. Ethereum, for example, has no max supply: its supply grows with validator rewards and shrinks as part of the fees gets burned.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/3/body: If the total value (market cap) stays the same but circulating supply **doubles**, the price per unit gets **cut in half**. On the flip side, **burning** means sending tokens to an address nobody has the key to, so supply drops for good. So price means nothing unless you look at supply.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/4/prompt: A token's circulating supply went from 100 million to 200 million, and its market cap stayed the same ($50 million). What did the price go from and to?
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/4/explanatio: Price = market cap ÷ supply. 50 ÷ 100 = $0.5 and 50 ÷ 200 = $0.25. Doubling the supply with the same demand cuts the price in half.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/5/pairs/0/me: Tokens you can trade on the market
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/5/pairs/1/me: All existing tokens, even locked ones
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/5/pairs/2/me: The final cap on the number of tokens
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/6/body: Of the **21 million** bitcoin, more than 90% have already been mined, and the rest will be mined at an ever-slowing pace until around **2140**. An estimated **several million bitcoin are lost forever** (their keys are gone), so the truly active supply is less than 21 million.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/7/sentence: When tokens get ___, supply goes down, and when new tokens get ___, supply goes up.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/7/explanatio: Burning takes tokens out of circulation forever, and minting creates fresh ones. Trading or transferring only changes who owns the token.
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/8/prompt: Which statement about Bitcoin's supply is true?
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/8/options/0: It's capped at 21 million, and part of that is lost forever
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/8/options/1: It's capped at 21 million, but the cap rises every 4 years
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/8/options/2: It's capped at 21 billion and grows every day
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/8/options/3: It has no cap, just like fiat money
lessons/onchain-u1-l1/steps/8/explanatio: The 21 million cap is written into Bitcoin's code. Every 4 years, only the pace of new coins is halved; the cap never changes. Lost coins also shrink the active supply.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/0/body: **Inflation** is how fast new tokens are added to the supply. If the supply is 100 million and 10 million new tokens arrive each year (staking rewards, mining or scheduled emissions), inflation is **10% a year**. For the price to hold steady, demand has to grow by about the same amount.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/1/prompt: A token's supply is 500 million, and 25 million new tokens are issued each year. What's the yearly inflation?
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/1/explanatio: 25 ÷ 500 = 0.05, so 5% yearly inflation. Every holder who isn't earning rewards gets diluted by 5% a year.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/2/body: Tokens for the team and early investors are usually **locked** and released on a **vesting** schedule. There's often a **cliff** first, say 12 months with no release at all, followed by a gradual release. On the day of a **big unlock**, the sellable supply suddenly jumps.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/2/tip: Before buying an altcoin, check its unlock calendar.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/3/statement: A big unlock of early investors' tokens can create selling pressure, since many of them bought at a much lower price.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/3/explanatio: An early investor who bought far lower makes a big profit even selling at today's price. They don't always sell, but the risk is real.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/4/prompt: On the candle marked "Unlock", 15% of the circulating supply was released. What does the chart show?
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/4/options/0/: Heavy-volume selling pressure after the release
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/4/options/1/: A price jump because supply shrank
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/4/options/2/: No change in volume or price
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/4/options/3/: The start of a strong uptrend
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/4/explanatio: Price was already weak before the unlock (many traders get out early), and on unlock day it dropped about 14% on several times the usual volume. An unlock increases supply; it doesn't reduce it.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/5/pairs/1/me: A period when no tokens are released
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/5/pairs/3/me: The rate new tokens join the supply
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/6/body: Some networks **burn** part of their fees. **Net inflation = new issuance − amount burned.** If burning outpaces issuance, supply becomes **deflationary**, like Ethereum's during periods when the network was very busy.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/7/prompt: A network issues 3 million new tokens a year and burns 4 million tokens from fees. What happens to supply?
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/7/options/0: It shrinks by 1 million a year (deflationary)
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/7/options/1: It grows by 7 million a year
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/7/options/2: It grows by 1 million a year
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/7/explanatio: Net inflation = 3 − 4 = −1 million. When burning outpaces issuance, supply shrinks every year.
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/8/prompt: In terms of supply pressure, which token is riskier?
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/8/facts/0/va: 40% inflation · 20% of supply unlocks next month
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/8/options/0: X; it has high inflation and a big unlock coming soon
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/8/options/1: Y, because most of its tokens are already released
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/8/options/3: Can't tell; supply has no effect on price
lessons/onchain-u1-l2/steps/8/explanatio: X gets diluted 40% every year and has a new wave of supply coming next month. Y has little future supply; that's no reason to buy it, but its supply pressure is lower.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/0/body: **FDV (fully diluted valuation) = price × max supply.** It shows what the project would be worth at today's price if every token were already on the market. **Market cap** only counts the **circulating supply**.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/1/prompt: A token's price is $0.5, its circulating supply is 400 million and its max supply is 2 billion. What's the FDV?
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/1/explanatio: FDV = 0.5 × 2 billion = $1 billion. $200 million is the market cap (0.5 × 400 million), just 20% of the full value.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/2/title: A big gap means future supply
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/2/body: When **market cap is far below FDV**, most tokens still have to enter the market. Just for the price to **stay flat**, new demand has to show up for all that future supply. These projects are called **"low float, high FDV"**.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/3/statement: If a token's market cap is $100 million and its FDV is $1 billion, then once all tokens are released, market cap has to grow 10x just for the price to stay the same.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/3/explanatio: At this price, all the tokens together are worth $1 billion. So market cap has to go from 100 million to 1 billion: 10 times the money, just to keep the price standing still.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/4/prompt: Which token faces more future supply pressure?
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/4/options/0: B; only 10% of its supply is circulating
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/4/options/1: A, because its market cap is bigger
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/4/options/3: A, because its FDV is close to its market cap
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/4/explanatio: About 91% of A's supply is circulating (500 of 550), but only 10% of B's (200 million of 2 billion). 90% of B's supply is still on the way.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/5/body: To compare projects, look at **market cap and FDV side by side**, and add the **unlock schedule** on top. A token with a "cheap" unit price but a multi-billion FDV isn't necessarily cheap. The price of one unit on its own tells you **nothing** about whether a token is cheap or expensive.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/6/sentence: FDV is price times ___, but market cap is calculated with ___.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/6/explanatio: FDV counts all future supply, while market cap counts only what can be traded right now.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/7/prompt: Order these tokens from highest to lowest market cap to FDV ratio.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/7/explanatio: The ratios are 90%, 50%, 20% and 5%. The lower the ratio, the more supply still has to enter the market.
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/8/prompt: A token just got listed. In 3 months, the team's first big unlock (100 million tokens) arrives. Which analysis makes more sense?
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/8/options/0: Circulating supply will triple; the risk of selling pressure is high
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/8/options/1: Market cap is only 50 million, so it's bound to grow
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/8/options/2: FDV doesn't matter; only the unit price does
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/8/options/3: The unlock reduces supply, so the price will rise
lessons/onchain-u1-l3/steps/8/explanatio: 50 + 100 = 150 million, so circulating supply triples. Market cap is only 5% of FDV, and most of the supply is still on the way. If you do get in, keep your size small and use a stop loss.
